key_insight: BLS-FALQON keeps the depth-reduction benefits of SO-FALQON while cutting measurement overhead by using a backtracking line-search-inspired control rule.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more hardware-efficient path for quantum optimization on near-term superconducting devices by reducing both circuit depth pressure and per-step measurement cost.
method: Replace SO-FALQON's second-order control update with a backtracking line search rule
Adapt FALQON to choose control coefficients with fewer measurements per step
Validate the tradeoff on combinatorial optimization instances and real hardware
evidence_signal: On max-cut problems with 8–20 vertices, simulations show a 37.7% reduction in total measurement count versus SO-FALQON, and experiments on the Tianyan-176 quantum computer confirm hardware viability.
watch_item: The approach still depends on iterative feedback measurements, so noise, finite sampling, and hardware calibration can affect performance.
paper_title: Feedback-based quantum optimization with low depth and measurement
